about: The epistola of the formulary “15th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: If we live in the Spirit, let us walk in the Spirit too. Let us not become eager for empty glory, provoking each other, envying each other. Brethren, even if a man is overtaken in some fault, you who are spiritual, instruct someone like this in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself, lest you too be tempted. Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ. For if anyone considers himself to be something, when he is nothing, he misleads himself. But let each one examine his own work, and then he will have his glory in himself alone, and not in another. For everyone will carry his own burden. Now let the one who is taught the word share in all good things with the one who teaches him. Do not go astray: God is not mocked. Whatever things a man has sown, these, indeed, he will also reap. For whoever sows in his flesh will also reap corruption from the flesh; but whoever sows in the spirit will reap eternal life from the spirit. And let us not falter in doing good, for in its own time we will reap, provided we do not falter. So then, as long as we have time, let us work what is good toward all, but above all toward those of the household of the faith.
